result: Aptamer serum proteomics in 54 ME/CFS vs 27 controls found 1823 of 7326 aptamers different (845 after FDR), with intracellular skeletal-muscle proteins particularly reduced.

result: In 88 hospitalised COVID-19 survivors at 4+ months, 34% had fatigue; fatigue was associated with higher serum myostatin and irisin and prior ICU admission (OR 2.65, 95% CI 1.03-6.94), with no differences in lung function, diaphragm/lung ultrasound or LV systolic function.
reason: Muscle/long COVID domain: resting serum myokines in post-hospital LC fatigue are not covered; possibly related to muscle-exertion-irisin-tsp1 but that concerns ME/CFS exertion, so not a direct match

result: In long-term PCS (~30 months), moderate-severe cases (n=27) had lower peak VO2 than mild (n=20) and asymptomatic post-COVID controls (n=48) (24.1 vs 26.7 vs 27.0 mL/kg/min), more chronotropic insufficiency (81.5% vs 35% vs 12.5%) and abnormal HRR, with no ventilatory limitation; CI and HRR did not correlate with peak VO2.
reason: Same measure (CPET peak VO2) in LC vs recovered controls, same direction, no ventilatory limit; smaller gap (~3 mL/kg/min) and small groups

result: Chronotropic insufficiency during CPET was found in 81.5% of moderate-severe vs 35% mild vs 12.5% asymptomatic post-COVID subjects, and abnormal HRR in 33% vs 20% vs 8%.
reason: Exercise chronotropic incompetence/HRR, not orthostatic testing or MSNA; this aspect is already covered by the sibling link to muscle-exertion-lc-peak-vo2

result: Same 192-subject cohort at ~1028 days post-infection: moderate-severe PCS had more symptoms during CPET (73.6% vs 24.8% vs 17.4%), failed to reach anaerobic threshold more often (51.8% vs 25% vs 12.5%) and had lower peak VO2 (24.1 vs 26.7 vs 27.0 mL/kg/min).
reason: Same measure and direction; note it is the same cohort and VO2 data as 40426965, so count once

result: Among 100,055 people with a G93.3 hospital record in England (0.16%), the female-to-male ratio was 3.88:1, peaking at about 6:1 in the fourth and fifth decades; estimated lifetime prevalence up to 0.92% in females and 0.25% in males.
reason: Large independent dataset on female preponderance, adds age-specific sex ratio; not in this finding's studies (already cited under trials-prevalence-sex)

result: 100,055 diagnosed with ME/CFS in England's Hospital Episode Statistics (0.16%), F:M 3.88:1, white people ~5x more likely to be diagnosed, wide regional variation (0.086-0.82% in females).
reason: already cited: Samms & Ponting 2025, BMC Public Health

result: In a phase 4 RCT, solriamfetol improved FSI fatigue severity vs placebo at week 8 (p=.039) but not week 6 (p=.270), and BRIEF-A global executive composite at week 8 (p=.012).
reason: already cited: preprint of Young 2025 J Psychopharmacol, the trial the finding describes

result: In N3C EHR data on 6.5 million adults, about half of patients labelled by a PASC computable phenotype were also labelled by an ME/CFS phenotype; dyspnea, fatigue and cognitive impairment were shared top predictors, with cardiopulmonary conditions more PASC-specific and pain/sleep more ME/CFS-specific.
reason: Measures overlap of EHR-coded phenotypes, not incidence of ME/CFS after infection; no atlas finding covers EHR phenotype overlap
